options.text: By burning fuels that contain nitrogen compounds
By nitrogen and oxygen from the air reacting together at high temperatures in engines and furnaces
By dissolving nitrogen gas in water

questions.explanation: Nitrogen oxides form when nitrogen (N2) and oxygen (O2) from the air react together at the very high temperatures found inside car engines and power station furnaces: N2 + O2 -> 2NO. The NO is then further oxidised to NO2 in the atmosphere. These gases cause acid rain and respiratory problems.

questions.stem: How do power stations remove sulfur dioxide from their exhaust gases?

options.text: By flue gas desulfurisation, using calcium oxide or calcium hydroxide to react with SO2
By burning the gas at higher temperatures
By dissolving it in water and releasing it into rivers

questions.explanation: Flue gas desulfurisation removes SO2 from power station exhaust by reacting it with calcium oxide or calcium hydroxide: CaO + SO2 -> CaSO3, or Ca(OH)2 + SO2 -> CaSO3 + H2O. This can remove up to 95% of SO2. The calcium sulfite product can be converted to gypsum for building materials.
